trial_title: Improving Coordination and Transitions of Care in Stroke Patients
brief_summary: This study will examine if the attending nurse model will enhance critical patient-centered elements of care that will in turn improve patient education and shared decision-making, medication adherence, stroke-related health literacy, and reduce early readmissions to ultimately yield improved patient quality of life. Our primary objective is to determine whether the attending nurse model of care improves stroke patients' health at 7 days, 30 days, and 90 days after hospital discharge as assessed

eligibility_table.criterion: Admission to the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania Vascular Neurology service
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is admitted to the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania Vascular Neurology service.
The information does not specify whether the hemorrhage is incident or recurrent.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced any incidents of recurrent spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage within the last 12 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: Ischemic stroke: focal neurological deficit of likely ischemic vascular origin
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has an intraventricular hemorrhage, not an ischemic stroke.

eligibility_table.criterion: Intracerebral hemorrhage: blood seen on initial head CT
eligibility_table.justification: Blood is seen on the initial head CT due to the spontaneous intraventricular hemorrhage.

eligibility_table.criterion: Transient Ischemic attack: focal neurological deficit of likely ischemic vascular origin that has clinically resolved
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a hemorrhagic event, not a transient ischemic attack.
There is no information provided about the patient's pregnancy status.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently pregnant or has she been pregnant within the last 12 months?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication that the patient is in comfort or hospice care.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been assessed for eligibility for hospice care based on a prognosis of less than 6 months to live?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding the patient's cognitive status prior to the stroke.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented diagnosis of severe dementia, defined as a score of ≤10 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)?

eligibility_table.criterion: Non-communicative and have no family/social support
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about the patient's communication ability or social support.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a Glasgow Coma Scale score of ≤8, indicating non-communicative status?
